summary: Somerset County, PA tower on Laurel Hill, erected 1934 and manned from 1935; sold to the Fish and Boat Commission in 1984, restored and padlocked; climbs only at staff-led events.

facts.agency: Pennsylvania DCNR, Laurel Hill State Park complex

staffing.status: not used as a lookout in living memory; last towerman named 1945

access.note: Padlocked; climbing only with park staff at scheduled events. The 2021 DCNR tour required registration and climbers had to be 18 or older.

visit.trail_note: A short hike to the tower, reached by a narrow path off Fire Tower Road near the Westmoreland-Somerset county line

events.note: Tower erected (Forest Lookouts); a March 1935 notice gives 80 feet and says ECW labor erected it
Towermen to be posted for the first time that spring; E. T. Beck named as towerman
A cabin for the towerman was contemplated at the summit; the sources do not say whether it was built
Observer in the tower spotted a fire near Bakersville, Somerset Township; it got out of control near Normalville, Fayette County, and destroyed a church and two dwellings
Martin Krepps named as towerman; the last towerman named in the sources
Deeded to the state Fish and Boat Commission, which used it as a mount for communications equipment
DCNR guided tour and short hike to climb the tower, registration required, climbers 18 and older

corrections.why: Kooser State Park is a park, not an agency; the article names DCNR as the overseeing body, and the DCNR listing places the tour at Laurel Hill State Park

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The March 1935 notice gives 80 feet (kept as 24.4 m); the Tribune-Review article gives 82 feet. The story reports both.
The Tribune-Review article calls the park Kooser State Park, while the DCNR tour listing says Laurel Hill State Park; the same DCNR ranger oversees both parks.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on height (80 ft in 1935, 82 ft in the TribLive article). They name the crew differently (ECW labor in 1935, CCC labor in TribLive), and no cached source says whether these are the same crew, so the story does not call the crew a disagreement. The state PA ArcGIS storymap (cached at data/raw/pa_storymap/data.json, script-only, not readable by fetch_text) credits the McClintock-Marshall Construction Company, gives 80 ft, and says the tower is maintained for controlled public access; it is not cited as evidence. The TribLive article carries no date in the copy read, so the 1984 deed and the restoration are undated; the restoration has no event entry for that reason. Park naming differs between sources. The Daily American 2015 article returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Check whether the tower is still padlocked and whether DCNR still runs climbs.
